chapter: The Dew Drop, Blue Eagle and visiting stars
title: Frank Painia's drinking and the Mobile gig split
summary: Frank Painia booked an Alabama gig and took a cut; Ridgley recalls keeping beans in the pot.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What do you think Frank thought of all this? Frank Panion?

Well, Frank, he would never see. You would talk to Frank in private, I guess he would say something. But most likely he would probably a little bit too drunk to say too much anyway. Yeah. He kept his liquor. Frank Panion, I don't know if we ever told you about this, but Frank had a drink. Anyway, he had to stop for five minutes. He had, oh yeah, he was, well, he's been allowed. He had a bottle somewhere. He had all kind of bottles. He said, I'll talk to him in the jar. He reached and pulled his drop. Check it out. Put it back in. And this was any time of the day? Any time of the day, any time of the night. Any time of the night. Any time you're talking, get him a lift. And he was very shrewd. I think I mentioned the time he sent me and the Aspiders. We went to Alabama to play. And he asked me how much I wanted. Anyway, he got me the $250. So that was good money to go to, go to, go to, with that Mobile. And he had the Spiders. I don't know how much they were getting, but I think it was four in the group. But anyway, we went to, we played the gig. No, he told me to go to Tom Couch. In, well, out now, anyway, he told me to go to Tom Couch. And Tom Couch was going to, tell me what to do. So I went on Tom Couch and he told me, he said, look, when you get there, after you finish playing, he said, they're going to give you envelope, so you stop back here. Okay. They gave me envelope and it wasn't sealed. And I went there for $250. And so, since it wasn't sealed, I looked in and it was a check for $750. I took this check to Tom Couch. And I, he took that and then he gave me another one. So since that had happened, I won't see. So I found a way to open that envelope. He had $250. The check was $500. That's his check. And so when I get to the dude drop, Frank Pena gave me $250. So he had $250. Now, I don't know how much the Spiders got. They might have got. They might have had a different thing. Or they might have got their money, you know, different. But anyway, Frank made $250. Tom Couch made $250. And I made $250. It's not a business. No, well, yeah, it was business. They made a business, you know. And like I said, $250 at that time was plenty of money. Plenty of money. Sure, I paid my band $20 a man, and $20 per man was plenty of money. That was good. Yeah. And you know, and whatever. I will say, you know, things have been fairly decent for me. I always was able to make a dollar here and there. And never, never, like I said, never really get rich. But I always kept some beans in the pot. And I always used that phrase because Benny Spellman could say it so good, you know. I didn't get the man, keep the beans in the pot, man. And that's what it was all about. And that's what it was all about.
What are some more things about Frank?
